entries.why_wrong: Swapping the order of `console.log(n)` and the recursive call only changes whether numbers print before or after deeper calls happen — it doesn't touch what makes recursion stop. The real problem is that nothing ever checks `n` and returns early, so the calls keep piling up regardless of when you log.

Counting up instead of down wouldn't fix anything here; the function would still call itself forever, just heading toward positive infinity instead of negative infinity. The missing piece is a base case that stops the recursion, not which direction `n` moves.

Whether `countdown` logs or returns a value is a separate design choice from whether it ever stops calling itself. Even a version that returns instead of logging would still recurse infinitely, because there's still no condition checking `n` and halting the calls.
